Prove times include commitment. Each 10-thread figure is the median of five proves: Aerie runs one batch per process after a warm-up process, as its CI does, and BitZ proves five times in one process after a warm-up prove. The single-thread figures come from the unprofiled runs the flamegraphs are scaled to; Aerie's single-thread verify is its own one-thread verifier pool in the same runs.

BitZ as shipped turns on its optimized binder only at 1, 8, 12 or 16 workers. At 10 workers its default path proves in {DEFAULT_PROVE} and verifies in {DEFAULT_VERIFY}. The table forces the optimized binder, the same code the single-thread flamegraph runs.

Aerie's verifier computes HashToPoint from the salts; BitZ verifies against targets it is given. Peak memory is the process's maximum resident set size on 10 threads, including inputs and verification.
